Five more review findings landed on docs/spec-opencode-integration.tex (from Qodo, a third reviewer, after Cursor/Copilot) — fold these into your current work before submitting, don't treat as a separate round:

1. **(Duplicate of what you're already fixing, extra confirmation)** `AllocateDelegationForkPropagated` never writes `claims'`, so forked sessions can't get trailers. Already in your brief.

2. **(Duplicate, extra confirmation)** The witness's own liveness/epoch isn't checked — already relayed to you in my prior message.

3. **NEW — `ForkSession` itself has the same restart-staleness gap.** `ForkSession`'s guard only checks `parentSid? \in \dom sessions` — it does NOT require the parent to be alive/corroborated in the current epoch. So after `RestartService`, a stale (pre-restart) parent can still spawn a live child, undermining `RestartClearsLiveness`'s intended guarantee at the fork step itself, not just at delegation-allocation. I verified this directly by reading `ForkSession`'s schema at line ~748. Fix: add the same liveness/epoch guard on `parentSid?` that `JoinSession`/other operations already require on their own session arguments.

4. **NEW — `ResolveCommitAttribution`'s case 3 may conflate two different situations.** The "candidate exists but is unusable" branch (session absent from registry, OR dead, OR wrong epoch, OR unclaimed) sets `diagnostic! = zfalse` (no diagnostic) uniformly. But an absent/dead/wrong-epoch candidate is arguably a genuine resolution FAILURE worth a diagnostic (case 2's territory — `sessionResolved?=ztrue` but the candidate turns out bad), while "candidate exists, alive, right epoch, but genuinely has no claim" is the normal unclaimed-session case where silence is correct. Review whether this case needs splitting into two, or whether the current single case is actually the right modeling choice — if you keep it as one case, add explicit justification prose for why an invalid/stale candidate and a valid-but-unclaimed one get the same silent treatment, since a reviewer reading just the schema will assume they're different situations by default.

5. **NEW, independent of 1-4 — `HarnessNeutrality` is literally false as currently worded.** The theorem states "no guard or effect predicate in any schema mentions the harness field at all." I grepped the document myself: `CorroborateSession`'s schema at line ~1036 has `rec?.harness = (sessions(sid?)).harness` — an explicit equality constraint ON the harness field. This is a real contradiction between the theorem's prose and its own proof content, confirmed by direct read, not a style nit. Fix: restate the theorem precisely — the actual property is likely "harness is only ever PRESERVED (compared for equality with itself / copied forward), never used to select different behavior or distinguish cases" — which is a real, true, and still useful property, just not literally "never mentioned." State it accurately.

Also, separately (not a content fix, FYI for your own context): `resolve.SessionID` does NOT have any process-tree-walk fallback — I verified directly in `internal/resolve/resolve.go:311-359`. It checks `ETHOS_SESSION` env, then `UnderClaudeCode()`, then requires a CORROBORATED PID (`ClaudePIDFromEnvCorroborated`) — if that fails, it returns an error, it does not walk anything. If your spec's §Harness Instantiation or scope section describes a process-tree walk as the fallback mechanism, that's wrong and should be corrected too — `ETHOS_SESSION` is the actual, already-existing harness-neutral integration seam, which is good news for the design, not bad. Check your own citations around this (the mission brief mentioned this file; verify what you actually wrote matches the real function behavior).

Same underlying cross-context problem you're already investigating — just another citation of it, at lines ~124-141 and ~441-460.

2. **NEW — worktree isolation claim rests on the wrong storage location.** The document places mission correlation state in a per-worktree `.punt-labs/ethos/missions/<id>/` tree, but `mission claim` actually writes `active-mission` under the user-GLOBAL `$HOME/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/<session-id>/` tree (this is directly confirmed by my own investigation this session into a related mission-log issue — I independently found `.punt-labs/local/ethos/missions/` is also per-checkout-but-not-the-tracked-tree, a related but distinct storage-location subtlety; verify the GLOBAL-sessions-tree claim yourself against `internal/mission/active.go`'s `ActiveMissionPath` function and `cmd/ethos/mission.go`). If a plugin follows the document's CURRENT description, the unchanged commit-msg hook will never read its correlation file, and worktree independence cannot actually be attributed to per-worktree directories as currently written. Fix: rewrite the worktree-isolation section around the real global, session-keyed sidecar path, and attribute worktree independence to distinct OpenCode session IDs instead.

3. **NEW — the proposed `mission claim` call can't resolve its own caller.** The `session.created` handler is described as calling `ethos mission claim <id>` without ever passing `--session <opencode-session-id>` or setting `ETHOS_SESSION` — so `runMissionClaim` has no way to resolve which caller it's binding for. This also affects the LATER committing shell: I independently verified `internal/resolve/resolve.go:311-359`'s `SessionID` function directly — it checks `ETHOS_SESSION` env FIRST, before anything else, with no process-tree-walk fallback at all (see finding 4 below, same underlying fact). So `ETHOS_SESSION` is the actual integration seam this document needs to specify explicitly: the plugin must set `ETHOS_SESSION=<opencode-session-id>` in the environment of both the `mission claim` subprocess AND whatever shell later runs the committing `git commit`, or the whole chain breaks. Fix: document this identity-propagation requirement explicitly for normal sessions, forks, and restarts.

4. **NEW, important, changes your framing — the document's own description of session resolution is wrong.** You (and the companion spec) describe `resolve.SessionID`/the commit-msg hook as falling back to a Claude-Code-ancestor process-tree WALK when no env override is set. I verified directly: the real function checks `ETHOS_SESSION` env, then requires a CORROBORATED PID lookup — if that fails, it returns an error. There is NO process-tree-walk fallback anywhere in this path. This is actually good news for your design, not bad: `ETHOS_SESSION` is already a harness-neutral seam that exists TODAY, with zero new ethos-side mechanism needed to use it for OpenCode — rewrite the relevant passages (wherever you describe "the hook walks the process tree") to describe the real chain accurately, and lean into `ETHOS_SESSION` as the integration point your bundled-plugin recommendation should use.

5. **NEW, Low severity but a real self-contradiction — press release claims the trailer miss is "silent" with "no channel to report."** `runHookCommitTrailers` actually prints a `ethos: commit-trailers: ...; no trailer added` diagnostic to stderr whenever a session was EXPECTED but couldn't be resolved — this is exactly what the companion spec's own `FailClosedOnAmbiguity`/diagnostic mechanism models. Under OpenCode specifically, it's silent only because the process isn't detected as "under Claude Code" at all (so no session was ever expected — a different case, not failed resolution). Fix: correct the press release's framing — the real story is "OpenCode isn't recognized as a session-bearing harness at all today, so no trailer AND no diagnostic fires, because the code's current model doesn't know to expect one" — not "git hooks have no channel to report," which is false of the actual code.

6. **NEW — real cross-repo conflict, informational, may not need a content fix.** The recommended `ethos enable --opencode` flow deposits an external OpenCode plugin, but `punt-labs/points` currently requires every active plugin to be built-in (would fail `points`' own `make doctor`/`make check-dev`). This may just need an explicit callout in the document (a known adoption blocker for one specific downstream consumer) rather than a design change — your call on whether this changes the recommendation or just needs disclosure.

These interact with what's already in your brief (finding 1 here duplicates your investigation into findings 1/3/6). Given how much is converging on the hook-plugin/CLI-plugin context-separation problem and the real `ETHOS_SESSION` mechanism, this may mean a genuinely different, more concrete fork/restart/claim-propagation design than what's currently written — don't preserve the current framing if these facts require real rework, which they likely do. Re-verify with markdownlint after. This is now a substantial second-pass correction, not a quick patch — take the time it needs.

tool_input.message:
Important correction to the design, not just another citation — verify this yourself via context7 before finalizing, since it changes the shape of the fix:

Copilot found, and I independently verified via context7 against `anomalyco/opencode`'s real source, that forking does NOT fire a generic `session.created` event. The actual source (`packages/core/src/session.ts`) publishes a DEDICATED event:

```typescript
yield* bus.publish(SessionEvent.Forked, {
  sessionID,
  parentID: parent.id,
  boundary: { type: input.before ? "before" : "through", messageID: boundary.id },
  ...inherited,
})
```

`SessionEvent.Forked` carries `parentID` DIRECTLY in its own payload — no `context.data.session.root`/`.family` lookup needed to discover a fork's lineage. The parent is right there in the event the plugin receives. I also confirmed the SDK's own `Session` type (v2) has an optional `parentID` field on every session object returned by `api.state.session.get(sessionID)`.

commit-msg hook resolves "whose session is this" via
`resolve.SessionID` (`internal/resolve/resolve.go:311-359`), which
checks an `ETHOS_SESSION` environment override first and otherwise

read, the function has **no process-tree-walk fallback at all**, an
earlier draft of this document said it did and was wrong. OpenCode
sets neither signal today, so `SessionID` returns `ErrNotUnderClaudeCode`
and the hook takes the "no session was ever expected" branch: no
trailer, and correctly **no diagnostic either**, because that branch
means "nothing was expected to happen here," not "something failed."
That is a different, narrower silence than this document's earlier
draft claimed -- `runHookCommitTrailers` DOES print a stderr diagnostic
(`ethos: commit-trailers: ...; no trailer added`) whenever a session
WAS expected and failed to resolve; it is not true that "a git hook has
no channel to tell the operator." The actual gap this integration
closes is narrower and more precise: OpenCode is not recognized as a
session-bearing harness at all today, so no session is ever expected
from it, and the silent branch -- correct for its own case -- fires
instead of the diagnostic branch that would fire for an ambiguous
Claude Code resolution failure.

commit-msg hook that stamps `Mission:`/`Delegation:` trailers. That
hook already runs independent of which process made the commit --

resolves a session via `resolve.SessionID` (`ETHOS_SESSION` env, then a
corroborated Claude PID -- no process-tree walk, confirmed by direct

**Corrected here, a real gap an earlier draft glossed over.** It is
not enough for the plugin to call `ethos mission claim <id>` with no
further argument. `runMissionClaim`
(`cmd/ethos/mission.go:2076-2129`) writes its active-mission sidecar
under the caller's OWN resolved session -- it does not register a new
OpenCode session with ethos, and it does not allocate a delegation.
And that sidecar lives under the user-GLOBAL,
session-ID-keyed `$HOME/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/<session-id>/` tree
(`internal/mission/active.go`'s `ActiveMissionPath`), not a per-worktree
file as an earlier draft of this FAQ claimed -- `resolve.SessionID`
reads `ETHOS_SESSION` from THAT process's environment, so setting it
only for the `mission claim` subprocess has no effect on a LATER
committing shell unless the SAME value is exported into that shell's
environment too. The actual requirement, stated precisely: the plugin
must (1) register the OpenCode session with ethos (allocating a
delegation under the active mission, not merely writing a bare
sidecar), and (2) export `ETHOS_SESSION=<opencode-session-id>` into the
environment of every subprocess OpenCode spawns for that session,
including whatever shell eventually runs `git commit` -- for example
via `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", ...)` setting the env on each
tool invocation, if OpenCode's own process model allows a plugin to
influence a spawned shell's environment this way (confirming that
mechanism is a prerequisite for this design, not assumed here). Only
once BOTH of those are true does "worktree independence" hold for
OpenCode the way it already holds for Claude Code -- it is a property
of each harness correctly keying its own session identity, not of
where a correlation file happens to live on disk.
